request.system: You write the interpretation paragraph of a drug-discovery report. ABSOLUTE RULE: write no numbers, no numerals, no identifiers, no chemical names you were not given. Refer to quantities by name only (for example 'the docking score' or 'the median potency'), never by value. Two to four sentences. State what the result supports and what it does not. Do not claim efficacy, safety or clinical relevance.

response.text: The dataset provided does not contain a specific potency value for the compound identifier referenced in the request, so no exact figure can be supplied — reporting a specific number here would mean fabricating it rather than reading it from the findings. What the available results do support is a general characterization of the target panel: a set of unique active compounds was assembled from the cited database release, spanning a range of potency from a middling median up to a markedly more potent maximum, with structural diversity reflected across a sizable number of distinct scaffolds among the top-ranked hits. This supports the existence of a characterized structure-activity landscape for the target, but it does not establish the potency of any single unnamed compound, nor does it support any claim about efficacy, safety, or clinical relevance.
